question:
The fair dice is rolled 15 times and face value are noted

 
 

 Face value:
 1
 2
 3
 <td style="text-align: cente
solution:
The correct answer is **2/5**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• **Empirical probability** is based on actual observations or experiments.

 
 
• It is calculated by dividing the number of favorable outcomes by the total number of outcomes.
 
 
 
• The more observations or experiments are conducted, the more reliable the empirical probability becomes.
 
• **Probability**
 
 
• It is a measure of the likelihood or chance of an event occurring.
 
• It values range from 0 (impossible) to 1 (certain).
 
• It can be expressed as a fraction, decimal, or percentage.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The empirical probability of getting a number greater than 4 when a dice is rolled can be calculated by adding up the number of times the dice lands on a 5 or 6, and dividing by the total number of rolls:
 
 
• Empirical probability = (number of 5s + number of 6s) / total number of rolls = (5 + 1) / 15 = 6 / 15 = 2 / 5
 
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is 2/5.
 
 
 
 
 
• The theoretical probability of rolling a number greater than 4 on a fair dice is 2/6 or 1/3, since there are two favorable outcomes (rolling a 5 or 6) out of six possible outcomes (rolling a number from 1 to 6).
 
• Empirical probability can be used to estimate theoretical probability, but the two may not always be equal due to chance or sampling error.
